title: 2018 Baulkham Hills Legal Studies Trial
notes: The PDF contains the complete 20-question multiple-choice section and no answer key. No shared stimuli or figures appear in the section.

questions.stem: Which of the following elements must be present for a murder charge to be proven?
questions.answerNote: Murder requires a prohibited act, the relevant mental element, and a causal link between the act and death.

questions.stem: VZ has been arrested for malicious wounding. Which of the following categories of crime does this offence come under?
questions.answerNote: Malicious wounding is a violent offence against an individual.

questions.stem: In which court are summary offences usually heard?
questions.answerNote: Summary offences are usually dealt with in the NSW Local Court.

questions.stem: The power to domestically enforce an international human rights treaty is found in which part of the Australian Constitution?
questions.answerNote: Section 51(xxix), the external affairs power, supports Commonwealth legislation implementing treaty obligations.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the Young Offenders Act 1997?
questions.answerNote: The Act provides alternatives such as warnings, cautions and youth justice conferences, emphasising diversion and rehabilitation.

questions.stem: Which of the following powers does the Coroner NOT possess?
questions.answerNote: A coroner investigates deaths and can compel evidence, but does not prosecute individuals.

questions.stem: What type of law in Australia best protects the right to vote?
questions.answerNote: Constitutional provisions, including the implied protection associated with representative government, underpin voting rights.

questions.stem: Under what conditions can a police officer legally search a person?

options.A: The police officer knows that the person is a criminal
options.B: The police officer wants to harass a person
options.C: The police officer believes that the person may be carrying a weapon or drug
options.D: The police officer believes that the person has been in prison

questions.answerNote: Police may conduct a search where statutory grounds exist, including reasonable suspicion that a person has a prohibited drug or weapon.

questions.stem: What type of right is the right to free speech?
questions.answerNote: Freedom of speech is generally classified as an individual civil and political right.

questions.stem: What is the term given for the crime where individuals or groups intend to overthrow the government by illegal means?
questions.answerNote: Treason/treachery (Criminal Code Cth s80.1, 80.1AC) cover intending/using force to overthrow the government; Sedition is urging others to do so (s80.2). Two plausible answers: B (treason) preferred, A (sedition) possible if the school's notes define sedition as overthrowing the government.

questions.stem: EA is attacked by a group of males wielding weapons. During the struggle EA kills one of the offenders. What is the most appropriate legal defence to this homicide?
questions.answerNote: The facts describe a response to an armed attack, supporting self-defence if the force used was reasonably necessary.

questions.stem: Who may apply to the Supreme Court for a Continuing Detention Order (CDO)?
questions.answerNote: The NSW Attorney General may apply to the Supreme Court for a continuing detention order under high-risk offender legislation.

questions.stem: Which of the following legal documents allows police to enter a dwelling?
questions.answerNote: A search warrant authorises police to enter premises for a specified investigative purpose.

questions.stem: What is an essential element for a person to be granted bail?

options.D: Agree to be willing to attend counselling

questions.answerNote: For prescribed serious offences, the Bail Act requires the accused to show cause why detention is not justified; This is the only listed bail-law concept.

questions.stem: Which of the following bodies can prosecute human rights offenders?
questions.answerNote: The ICC prosecutes individuals for international crimes including genocide, crimes against humanity and war crimes.

questions.stem: EZ has shown no remorse after being convicted of committing a crime where weapons were used and the victim was very old. What would these factors would be considered as?
questions.answerNote: Use of a weapon, victim vulnerability and lack of remorse are aggravating sentencing considerations.

questions.stem: Which of the following involves judicial discretion?
questions.answerNote: Judges exercise discretion when selecting a sentence within the applicable legal limits.

questions.stem: The term universal suffrage refers to?

options.A: The right to a fair trial

questions.answerNote: Universal suffrage is the right of adult citizens to vote, subject to limited lawful qualifications.

questions.stem: KA has been sentenced to 4 years in prison for assault causing grievous bodily harm. He is released after serving 3 years and 2 months. What is the term given to this early release?
questions.answerNote: Release before the full sentence has been served, subject to conditions, is parole.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the imposition of a sentence of life imprisonment?
questions.answerNote: Life imprisonment keeps an offender in custody for a long period or for life, principally protecting the community through incapacitation.
